note: A short, hand-written summary of the world at each snapshot, shown under the year in the overview. Keep each to two or three sentences of broad, well-established history. Keys are snapshot years (negative = BCE).

summaries.-123000: Modern humans live in Africa, while Neanderthals and other archaic humans inhabit Europe and Asia. The last interglacial is warmer than today, with hippos in the Thames and forest far into the north.
summaries.-10000: The last Ice Age is ending. Hunter-gatherers have reached every continent but Antarctica, mammoths are dwindling, and in the Fertile Crescent people are beginning to gather and tend wild grains.
summaries.-8000: Farming has begun in the Fertile Crescent, with wheat, barley, sheep and goats, and settlements like Jericho and Çatalhöyük grow. Rising seas are drowning Doggerland and the Bering land bridge.
summaries.-5000: Farming spreads across Europe, the Nile and Indus valleys and China, where rice and millet are grown. The Sahara is still green, dotted with lakes, herders and their cattle.
summaries.-4000: The first towns of Sumer rise in southern Mesopotamia, and the wheel and plough appear. On the steppe, people are taming the horse; in the Sahara, the wet period is coming to an end.
summaries.-3000: Writing begins in Sumer and Egypt, and Egypt is united under its first pharaohs. Bronze working spreads, and Stonehenge's first circle is raised on Salisbury Plain.
summaries.-2000: Old Babylonian and Egyptian Middle Kingdom civilisations flourish, while the Indus cities decline. Minoan palaces stand on Crete, and the Xia era unfolds along the Yellow River.
summaries.-1500: The New Kingdom makes Egypt an empire reaching into the Levant; Hittites, Mitanni and Babylon contend for the Near East. The Shang rule in China, writing on oracle bones.
summaries.-1000: After the Late Bronze Age collapse, new peoples and kingdoms emerge: Israel, the Phoenician cities, Assyria's revival. The Zhou have replaced the Shang, and iron spreads across Eurasia.
summaries.-700: Assyria dominates the Near East, Greek city-states found colonies across the Mediterranean, and Rome is a small Latin town. The Olmec and Chavín cultures thrive in the Americas.
summaries.-500: The Persian Empire is the largest the world has seen. Athens experiments with democracy, Rome has become a republic, and the Buddha and Confucius are teaching.
summaries.-400: Greece is exhausted by the Peloponnesian War, Persia still holds the east, and China is in its Warring States period. In India, the kingdom of Magadha is rising.
summaries.-323: Alexander the Great has just died in Babylon, leaving an empire from Greece to the Indus that his generals will carve up. Greek culture spreads across the Near East.
summaries.-300: Alexander's successors rule Hellenistic kingdoms from Egypt to Bactria. The Maurya Empire unites most of India, and Rome is mastering Italy.
summaries.-200: Rome has defeated Hannibal and turns east. The Han dynasty unites China after the brief Qin, and the Xiongnu rule the steppe to its north.
summaries.-100: Rome rules the Mediterranean but is torn by civil wars. Han China reaches west to Central Asia, and the Silk Road links the two ends of Eurasia.
summaries.-1: Augustus rules the Roman Empire at the height of its peace, and the Han rule China. Between them lie Parthia and the Kushan lands; together these empires hold about half the world's people.
summaries.100: The Roman Empire is near its greatest extent under Trajan, and Han China is its equal in the east. Teotihuacan is becoming one of the largest cities in the world.
summaries.200: Rome still holds its frontiers, but Han China is collapsing into the Three Kingdoms. In the Americas, the Maya build their first great cities.
summaries.300: The Roman Empire is reorganised under Diocletian and soon Constantine, who will favour Christianity. China is divided, and the Gupta era is about to begin in India.
summaries.400: Huns press on the steppe frontiers and Germanic peoples cross the Rhine and Danube; the Western Roman Empire is weakening. India flourishes under the Guptas.
summaries.500: The Western Roman Empire has fallen to Germanic kingdoms, while the Eastern (Byzantine) Empire endures. Teotihuacan and the Maya cities thrive.
summaries.600: The Sui reunite China, Byzantium and Sasanian Persia are locked in war, and in Arabia, Muhammad is about to begin preaching Islam.
summaries.700: The Umayyad Caliphate stretches from Spain to the Indus. Tang China is at its height, and Byzantium holds Anatolia and the Balkans.
summaries.800: Charlemagne is crowned emperor in the West, the Abbasids rule from Baghdad, and the Tang still govern China. Viking raids are beginning.
summaries.900: The Abbasid Caliphate is fragmenting, Tang China has fallen, and the Maya lowland cities are being abandoned. Vikings settle from Ireland to Kiev.
summaries.1000: Song China is the richest state on earth, the Holy Roman Empire and Byzantium dominate Europe, and the Fatimids rule Egypt. Norse sailors have reached North America.
summaries.1100: The First Crusade has taken Jerusalem, the Seljuk Turks rule much of the Middle East, and Song China prospers. Angkor is building its greatest temples.
summaries.1200: Genghis Khan is about to unite the Mongols. The Crusader states are shrinking, the Song have lost the north to the Jin, and Cahokia is past its peak.
summaries.1279: The Mongol Empire, now divided into khanates, spans from Korea to Hungary; this year it completes the conquest of Song China. Venice and Genoa trade across the Mediterranean.
summaries.1300: The Mongol khanates still rule most of Asia, the Mali Empire controls the gold of West Africa, and the Ottomans are a small beylik in Anatolia.
summaries.1400: Europe is recovering from the Black Death. Ming China sends great fleets into the Indian Ocean, Timur ravages Central Asia, and the Aztecs and Incas are rising.
summaries.1492: Columbus reaches the Caribbean, and Granada falls, ending Muslim rule in Spain. The Ottomans hold Constantinople, and the Inca and Aztec empires are at their height.
summaries.1500: Portugal has found the sea route to India and claimed Brazil, and the Spanish are settling the Caribbean. The Ottomans, Safavids and Ming dominate Asia.
summaries.1530: Spain has conquered the Aztecs and is invading the Inca. The Reformation divides Europe, the Mughals have taken North India, and the Ottomans have besieged Vienna.
summaries.1600: Spain and Portugal hold empires on several continents, while the Dutch and English East India companies are founded. The Ottoman, Safavid and Mughal empires are near their height.
summaries.1650: The Thirty Years' War has ended, and the Qing are conquering China from the Ming. European colonies dot the coasts of the Americas, Africa and Asia.
summaries.1700: Louis XIV's France dominates Europe, Russia is modernising under Peter the Great, and the Mughal Empire reaches its greatest extent before its decline.
summaries.1715: The War of the Spanish Succession has ended and Louis XIV has died. Britain is rising as a sea power, while the Mughals begin to fragment.
summaries.1783: The United States has won independence from Britain. Britain is expanding in India, Russia has annexed Crimea, and the Qing rule their largest empire.
summaries.1800: Napoleon rules France and is reshaping Europe by war. The British East India Company controls much of India, and Spain still holds most of Latin America.
summaries.1815: Napoleon is defeated and the Congress of Vienna redraws Europe. Latin America is fighting for independence, and Britain is the leading world power.
summaries.1878: Germany and Italy are newly unified states, the Ottoman Empire is losing the Balkans, and Britain rules India directly. Industrial railways and steamships are shrinking the world.
summaries.1880: European empires are about to partition Africa, the United States is settling the West, and Japan is modernising rapidly under the Meiji emperor.
summaries.1900: Africa has been carved up by European powers, the Qing face the Boxer Rebellion, and the British Empire covers a fifth of the world's land.
summaries.1914: The First World War begins. European empires rule most of Africa and much of Asia, while the Ottoman, Austro-Hungarian and Russian empires enter their final years.
summaries.1920: The war has destroyed four empires. New states emerge in Europe, the Soviet Union is forming, and the League of Nations has been founded.
summaries.1930: The Great Depression grips the world. The Soviet Union industrialises under Stalin, Japan is expanding in China, and fascism is rising in Europe.
summaries.1938: Nazi Germany has annexed Austria and the Sudetenland, Japan is at war in China, and Spain is in civil war. A second world war is a year away.
summaries.1945: The Second World War has ended with Germany and Japan defeated. The United Nations is founded, and the United States and Soviet Union emerge as superpowers.
summaries.1960: Decolonisation is sweeping Africa and Asia; seventeen African countries become independent this year. The Cold War divides the world into rival blocs.
summaries.1994: The Soviet Union has dissolved into fifteen states, Germany is reunited, and apartheid has ended in South Africa. Yugoslavia is breaking apart in war.
summaries.2000: Nearly two hundred sovereign states cover the map. Globalisation and the internet connect the world, while the European Union prepares to expand east.
summaries.2010: The world has about seven billion people. China is a rising economic power, South Sudan will soon become the newest state, and the Arab Spring is about to begin.
